newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1997 copper demand seen at 1.2 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: China 1997 copper demand seen at 1.2 mln tonnes.

text.p: China's demand for copper is expected to reach 1.2 million tonnes this year, up five percent from 1996, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The newspaper, published by the China Daily, said demand will be buoyed by steady economic growth coupled with government efforts to boost the domestic housing construction as well as the telecommunications industry.
It also said domestic output would be about 900,000 tonnes compared with the 909,700 tonnes produced last year. Raw material shortfalls would curb domestic copper production, it said.
The 1996 copper output total was up 5.7 percent over the previous year, according to official statistics.
Business Weekly said that China amassed a 170,000 tonne stockpile of copper last year and that would be used to fill some of the gap between domestic supply and demand.
It put imports at more than 130,000 tonnes this year.

The newspaper also said aluminium output is expected to reach 1.8 million tonnes while demand would be 1.9 million tonnes. Domestic consumption would be aided by growth in demand for use in construction, cars and motorcycles and telecommunications.
It said aluminium exports would rise while imports would remain at last year's levels. It gave no further details.
Zinc output is not expected to rise sharply this year from last year's levels while demand is seen making steady advances. Lead output is expected to increase slightly, it said.
The newspaper also said that the operation of more tinplate production lines would create additional demand of 2,000 tonnes of tin this year. It gave no further deatils.
